title: Shiv Kumar Yadav v. State of U.P.
coram: Naheed Ara Moonis, J.; Vivek Varma, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; remaining billing grievance relegated to clause 7.10.
headnote: After the Executive Engineer decided the consumer's representation against a demand notice and recovery citation, the High Court dismissed the writ and left any further billing grievance to the competent authority under clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Clauses 5.6 and 6.5, invoked in the prayer for a corrected bill on a new meter, were not construed.
facts: Shiv Kumar Yadav challenged a demand notice dated 1 August 2019 issued by the Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution-II, Mughalsarai, U.P. Power Corporation Limited, Chandauli, and a recovery citation dated 1 October 2019 issued by the Tehsildar, Mughalsarai. He sought a mandamus for a correct bill on a newly installed meter under clauses 5.6 and 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. After adjournments, counsel for the Power Corporation produced an order dated 30 September 2020 on the petitioner's representation of 13 January 2020.

holding_units.topic: forum after executive engineer decides billing representation
holding_units.holding: Where the Executive Engineer has already considered the consumer's representation against a demand notice and recovery citation, any remaining billing grievance is to be taken to the competent authority under clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the writ is dismissed.

principle_tags.application: After the Executive Engineer decided the petitioner's representation on the demand and recovery, the Court dismissed the writ and left further billing grievance to the clause 7.10 forum.
The Court treated clause 7.10 as the remaining statutory route once respondent No. 2 had already passed an order on the representation.
